question: Describe in words the function and the output of the following subroutine. SUBROUTINE GCD (I,J,K) IF (I - J) 1,4,2 1 L = J J = I I = L 2L = I-(I/J){_\ast}J IF(L) 3,4,3 3 I = J J = L GO TO 2 4 K = J RETURN END
options: The program finds the greatest common divisor K of two positive integers I and J.
The program calculates the least common multiple of I and J.
The program calculates the arithmetic mean of I and J and stores the result in K.
The program determines if I is a multiple of J and stores the boolean result in K.
The program adds I and J and stores the result in K.

The program multiplies I and J and assigns the product to K.
The program subtracts J from I and stores the result in K.
The program generates a random number between I and J and assigns it to K.
The program computes the sum of all integers between I and J and assigns it to K.
model_outputs:
This subroutine finds the greatest common divisor of the three positive integers I, J, and K.
The algorithm works as follows:
1. It first checks if I is equal to J. If so, the greatest common divisor is simply I (line 1).
2. If I is not equal to J, it checks if I is greater than J. If so, it updates I and J to be I and J respectively (lines 2 and 3).
3. It then calculates the greatest common divisor of I and J using Euclid's algorithm (lines 4-10).
4. Finally, it assigns the greatest common divisor to K (line 11).
The output of the subroutine is the greatest common divisor of the three input integers.

question: Which one of the following is equal to P(A, B, C) given Boolean random variables A, B and C, and no independence or conditional independence assumptions between any of them?

P(A | B) * P(B | C) * P(C | A, B)

question:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite directed acyclic graph with |E| > 0. Which of the following must be true?
I. G has a vertex with no incoming edge.
II. G has a vertex with no outgoing edge.
III. G has an isolated vertex, that is, one with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge.
options: I and III only
None of the above
I and II only
II and III only
I, II, and a vertex with one outgoing edge
I, II, and a vertex with one incoming edge
All of the above (I, II, III)
II only
I only
III only
model_outputs:
A directed acyclic graph (DAG) has no cycles.
- If a vertex has no incoming edge, it must be the source of at least one edge (it can be the source of multiple edges). So, I is true.
- If a vertex has no outgoing edge, it cannot be the target of any edge. So, II is true.
- An isolated vertex is a vertex with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge. So, III is true.
Therefore, the answer is (G).

question: Given image \begin{tabular}{|llll|} \hline 7 & 1 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 7 & 6 \\ 6 & 6 & 5 & 7 \\ \hline \end{tabular} , and the bit-depth of the image is 4. model_outputs:
The appropriate threshold value is the value that divides the cumulative histogram of the image into two equal parts.
The cumulative histogram of the given image is:
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|} \hline Intensity & Frequency \\ \hline 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 \\ 5 & 1 \\ 6 & 3 \\ 7 & 4 \\ \hline \end{tabular}
The middle value of the cumulative histogram is the threshold value. In this case, the middle value is 6. The answer is (F).
